description: The delivery key for a first send is a pure function of approval_id, action_id, draft_id, channel and normalised recipient.
why_it_exists: The WF4 outbound delivery key was once derived with $now in the basis, so a second attempt at the same approved delivery produced a different send_key and a different communication_id. An uncertain send result (a timeout after the message had actually gone) therefore resolved to a brand new row on retry, and the same letter could be sent to an insurer twice with no duplicate detectable anywhere in the register. This case pins the five stable fields and their order in the key basis.

expect.note: The original oracle hashes were computed by a separate Python FNV-1a implementation over the REAL recipient address. That address has been replaced by a same-length synthetic address, so the expected hash must be regenerated from this input with an independent FNV-1a implementation before this assertion means anything. Do not copy the value the JavaScript under test produces. The original assertions were send_key === "SND-d7ea6fb4" and communication_id_send === "COM-d7ea6fb4" for recipient insurer@<real-domain>.

assertions: delivery_key_parts is exactly "apr=APR-001 act=ACT-001 draft=DFT-001 chan=GMAIL to=insurerclaims01@example.com"
send_key is "SND-" + fnv1aHex(delivery_key_parts), verified against an independently implemented FNV-1a rather than against the code under test
